entries.description: How many bytes per second the device reads through its texture units, which take a different path to memory than plain buffer reads. Each pixel of the image is read exactly once, so caching cannot flatter the number.
entries.metric_description: Each fetch returns one whole pixel -- four 32-bit colour values, 16 bytes.

entries.description: How fast data crosses between the host's memory and the device's. On a discrete card that means the PCIe link, which is far narrower than either side's own memory and is what makes moving data to the device worth avoiding; where the two share one pool of memory the numbers are much higher. Both readings use pinned host memory, the fast path.
entries.metric_description: Host to device: sending data across to the device.

entries.metric_description: Device to host: reading results back. Often a little slower than the other direction.

entries.description: The overhead of asking the device to do anything at all. It is what small, frequent jobs pay before any of their own work begins.
entries.metric_description: One way only: from the moment the host queues the work to the moment the device starts running it.
